subject: Cloud Computing
title: Facebook's Six-Hour Disappearance
description: A quick win: understand Facebook's Six-Hour Disappearance.

hook.text: On October 4, 2021, Facebook, Instagram, and WhatsApp vanished for six hours. 3.5 billion users were affected.

buildup.text: A routine maintenance command accidentally withdrew Facebook's BGP routes — the internet's address book entries.

discovery.text: Without BGP routes, the internet couldn't find Facebook's servers. It was as if they didn't exist.

twist.text: Engineers couldn't fix it remotely because their own tools were down. They had to physically enter data centers.

climax.text: The outage cost Facebook an estimated $100 million in revenue and exposed the fragility of centralized platforms.

punchline.text: Facebook deleted itself from the internet. By accident.

quiz.question: Why couldn't Facebook engineers fix the outage remotely?
options: Their own remote access tools depended on the same infrastructure that was down
The engineers were all on vacation that day
Facebook's source code was accidentally deleted

details.summary: In October 2021, Facebook, Instagram, and WhatsApp went offline for over six hours after a BGP configuration change accidentally withdrew Facebook's network routes from the internet. Employees could not even enter buildings because internal systems also failed.
details.whyItMatters: Facebook's outage demonstrated how a single networking misconfiguration can take down an entire company. The cascading internal failures showed the danger of depending on your own services for recovery.
takeaways: A BGP change made Facebook unreachable on the internet
Internal tools failed too, preventing quick recovery
The outage lasted over six hours affecting billions of users

faq.question: What is BGP and how did it cause the outage?
faq.answer: BGP is the protocol that tells internet routers how to reach different networks. A configuration change accidentally withdrew Facebook's BGP routes, making its entire network invisible to the internet. Without valid BGP routes, no traffic could reach Facebook's servers.

faq.question: Why did recovery take so long?
faq.answer: Facebook's internal communication tools, building access systems, and management consoles all depended on the same infrastructure that was down. Engineers had to physically travel to data centers and gain manual access to equipment to begin restoring service.
